stem:
A student investigates a circuit containing resistors and a metal wire as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Resistors *Y* and *Z* have resistances *Y* and *Z* respectively.

The student connects a resistor of resistance *R* between P and Q.

The student then adjusts the length of the wire between the crocodile clips until the voltmeter reads zero. The student measures the length *L* of wire between the crocodile clips.

The student repeats the experiment with different values of *R*.

It is suggested that *L* and *R* are related by the equation

$\dfrac{Z}{R}=\dfrac{4\rho L}{\pi Yd^2}$

where *d* is the diameter of the wire and *ρ* is the resistivity of the metal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of *L* on the y-axis against $\dfrac{1}{R}$ on the x-axis.

Determine an expression for the gradient.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *R* and *L* are given in Table 2.1. Each resistance value *R* has a percentage uncertainty of ±5%.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of $\dfrac{1}{R}$ / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹ in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in $\dfrac{1}{R}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of *L* / cm against $\dfrac{1}{R}$ / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹.

Include error bars for $\dfrac{1}{R}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The student measures the diameter of the wire. The student’s values are:

0.263 mm     0.262 mm     0.263 mm     0.257 mm     0.262 mm     0.259 mm.

Determine the average diameter *d*. Include the absolute uncertainty in *d*.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
Resistors *Y* and *Z* each have a resistance of 22 Ω ± 5%.

Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (d), determine the value of *ρ*. Include an appropriate unit.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: Determine the resistance *R* that would give a value of *L* of 95.0 cm. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A circuit with resistors Y and Z, a battery, a voltmeter, and a metal wire connected by crocodile clips with the length L marked.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for R / Ω, 1/R / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹, and L / cm, with values in the first and third columns and blank cells in the middle column.
A blank graph grid with L / cm on the vertical axis and 1/R / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹ on the horizontal axis.
